newsitem.title: CHINA: Property profits to boost Swire interims.
newsitem.headline: Property profits to boost Swire interims.

text.p: Property development profits from Swire Pacific Ltd's Island Place project on Hong Kong Island are expected to boost the conglomerate's first-half 1997 earnings, analysts said on Tuesday.
Swire Pacific is due to announce the results on Thursday.
It posted net profit of HK$3.06 billion in the first six months of 1996, with a HK$468.0 million gain on the sale of part of the group's stake in Hong Kong Dragon Airlines Ltd.

"They will see bookings from the Island Place office and residential, and that should allow them to grow development earnings quite substantially. That is going to be the main driver," said Lehman Brothers analyst Philip Tulk.
He forecast earnings per share of HK$2.13 compared with HK$1.927 in the first six months of 1996.
Anil Daswani, an analyst at Salomon Brothers, said property development should contribute about HK$930 million to net profit, which he forecast at HK$3.7 billion.
"Despite the fact the aviation income will not be so large and there is no exceptional from the disposal of a stake in Dragonair, they will be booking income from development properties," he said.

Analysts expected Swire Pacific's 43.97 percent owned Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd unit to report disappointing first-half results, after it had to suspend its Airbus A330-300 service and suffered a decline in Japanese traffic.
"The dark side will be Cathay," said Anne Gardini at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett. But she said that should not surprise investors. "I think they have sent sufficient signals on that."
Swire Pacific chairman Peter Sutch said he expected the grounding in late May of the Airbus fleet to slice between HK$120 million and HK$150 million from the airline's bottom line this year.

Daswani said Swire shares were looking cheap after suffering from concerns about Swire's diminishing land bank which the company addressed with the purchase of the development rights for the former Shui Wing Steel mill site in Hong Kong.

"I am reasonably happy with the stock. I have a buy on it," he said. "I have got them making HK$8.45 billion in 1997, which is not that much in growth but then again there was a big exceptional in 1996 from the airline stuff," he said.
Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities, said there may be some profit-taking after the results are announced. He forecast 15 percent growth in interim net profit.
"The share price might retest HK$70.00," he said.
Swire Pacific shares fell HK$0.50 to HK$73.00 on Tuesday.
